Developer Dossier frames your portfolio as a confidential professional file — structured, authoritative, and precise. The design borrows visual language from classified documents and intelligence briefings, giving your work a commanding, serious edge. It suits developers who want to project expertise and leave a memorable first impression.

## Theme Overview

Developer Dossier builds its identity around the visual conventions of a classified professional file. Content is organized into clearly delineated sections that read like briefing panels — projects become case entries, skills become capability assessments, and contact details read like a field summary. The typography is crisp and document-weight, and the layout prioritizes legibility and hierarchy over decoration.

## Design Highlights

- **Color palette:** Dark neutrals with restrained accent tones that suggest official documentation
- **Typography:** Clean, authoritative typefaces with strong hierarchy and document-style spacing
- **Layout:** Panel-based structure organized like a multi-section classified file
- **Key UI elements:** Dossier-style content blocks, structured section headers, formal credential-like labels
- **Overall mood:** Polished, professional, and confidently technical

## Who This Theme Suits

Developer Dossier is an excellent fit for senior engineers, technical leads, and backend developers who want a portfolio that communicates depth and authority. It also works well for security researchers, DevOps professionals, and systems engineers who value precision and want their work presented with the same rigor they bring to their craft.
